old_description: Since 1978, we've proudly served the Central Oregon community, building lasting relationships and providing the equipment you need to get the job done right. about:
Central Oregon Forklift and Equipment has operated from Bend, Oregon since 1978 as a family-owned dealership serving the Central Oregon region. The business was founded on a commitment to build lasting relationships and treat every customer like family, a principle that continues to guide its operations today.

The company functions as a full-service equipment dealer, offering new and pre-owned forklifts, tractors, zero-turn mowers, implements, and attachments from brands such as Yale, LS Tractor, Kioti, and Bad Boy Mowers. Beyond sales, it provides equipment rentals, a parts department, and both mobile and in-shop repair services including preventative maintenance. Financing options are also available to support purchases.

Its customer base spans construction contractors, agricultural operators, landscapers, and property owners throughout Central Oregon. A testimonial from SunWest Builders highlights same-day on-site repair for a construction job site, while individual buyers in communities like La Pine rely on the dealership for tractors and mowers suited to rural property maintenance.

The company emphasizes responsive support to minimize downtime, promoting mobile technicians, flexible rental terms, and a service-first approach rooted in its family-owned heritage. It positions itself as a partner that keeps Central Oregon working through dependable equipment and straightforward guidance.

name: Century Mold
old_description: Century Mold delivers precision-engineered plastic solutions across North America
about:
Century Mold was founded in 1986 in Shelbyville, Tennessee. The company operates as a U.S.-based manufacturer of precision plastic components, serving customers across North America from six production facilities.

The company provides fully integrated services from part and tool design through production and finishing. Its capabilities include injection molding on presses up to 2,200 tons, vertical and horizontal molding, multi-material (two-shot and overmold), insert molding, gas-assist, and MuCell processes. Secondary operations cover assembly, balancing, vibration welding, sonic welding, hot plate welding, heat stake welding, pad printing, and performance testing. Engineering support encompasses design for manufacturability, Moldflow and finite element analysis, reverse engineering, scanning, and 3D printing. The facilities total 675,000 square feet and house more than 200 presses, supported by a team of over 50 engineers, designers, and mold builders.

Century Mold serves automotive, defense, industrial, consumer, and lawn-and-garden markets. In automotive, it supplies complex, high-volume components found in over 80 percent of vehicles on U.S. roads, working with OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers such as BorgWarner, Robert Bosch, Delphi, and Visteon. For defense, it provides mission-critical parts with secure, fully controlled U.S. production. Industrial and consumer customers rely on its in-house design and engineering expertise to bring products to market.

The company emphasizes a localized supply chain and in-house expertise to deliver consistent quality, on-time performance, and cost efficiency. It holds ISO 9001:2015 and IATF 16949 certifications and has earned multiple Supplier of the Year awards from major automotive OEMs.

Century Wire Products Corp. was established in 1998 in Wind Gap, Pennsylvania, drawing on more than 45 years of wire-industry experience. The company is 100 percent woman-owned, founded by Danielle, who relocated the operation from Washington to Wind Gap in 2009, bringing many employees with her.

The Pennsylvania plant manufactures stainless steel lashing wire, single-end wire, and messenger strand to standard specifications, with certification available on request. It also supplies galvanized EHS Class A strand meeting ASTM A475, both domestic and imported. The facility stocks all major sizes for same-day or next-day shipping, handles custom orders to customer specifications, and operates with EDI capability under ISO 9001:2015 certification.

Primary markets are CATV, telecommunications, and industrial sectors. Customers include contractors and broadband builders who must meet Build America, Buy America requirements. The company supports industry scholarship programs through the Cable Television Engineers Society, the Walter Katz Scholarship Foundation, the Missouri Cable Technical Association, and the Society of Cable Television Engineers.

Danielle's leadership emphasizes employment opportunities for people with disabilities through a long-standing partnership with Abilities of Northwest Jersey, earning recognition from ACCESS NJ and DiversityBusiness.com. The firm's differentiation rests on domestic manufacturing, rapid fulfillment from stock, and a woman-owned, WBENC-certified structure that aligns with federal procurement goals.

name: Certified Parts Corporation
old_description: Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft, with a mission to preserve well known international and local legacy brands that were in danger of extinction.  Initially specializing in manufacturing service parts for these companies, CPC has grown into a major supplier to OEM’s and has brought some of these brands back into production. Comet, TecumsehPower, Wisconsin Wagon and vintage recreational vehicle parts makeup CPC’s current lineup of companies.  CPC owns motorcycles and mini-cycle brands that include Bridgestone and Indian, Rupp, Chaparral and Steen along with a complimentary selection of hard-to-get engine parts that were used in many of the snowmobiles and mini-cycles of the day. A passion for history and recognizing opportunity serves as a guiding principle for Certified Parts Corporation.
about:
Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft in Edgerton, Wisconsin. The company traces its roots to 1974 when Grafft worked at Fox Corporation in Janesville and recognized the need for continuous parts supply for manufacturers that had ceased operations. In 1976 he purchased Fox's service-parts division and the Bridgestone brand on his 26th birthday. Two years later, Grafft established CPC with a mission to preserve well-known international and local legacy brands facing extinction, beginning with the acquisition of Arctic Cat's snowmobile division, including tooling, dies, intellectual property and trademarks.

Today CPC operates a 200,000-square-foot factory in Edgerton where it manufactures original service parts — carburetors, the full line of Comet torque converters and clutches, and other components — for a portfolio that includes Comet, TecumsehPower, Wisconsin Wagon, and vintage recreational-vehicle brands. The company also owns historic motorcycle and mini-cycle marques such as Bridgestone, Indian, Rupp, Chaparral and Steen, and supplies hard-to-find engine parts for snowmobiles and mini-cycles. Production volumes support both OEM contracts and aftermarket distribution through a worldwide dealer network.

CPC serves OEM manufacturers in the recreational, construction, agricultural and marine sectors, as well as dealers and end users maintaining vintage equipment. Its customer base includes original equipment builders that integrate Comet clutches into new products and a global service network that supports TecumsehPower, Lauson and Snow King engines.

The business was built on a passion for history and an eye for opportunity: Grafft's strategy of acquiring orphaned brands, restarting production and re-establishing dealer channels has returned multiple legacy names to active manufacturing.

name: Champlain Cable Corporation
old_description: Champlain Cable manufactures copper and aluminum wire and tubing. Based in upstate New York, products include building wire, refrigerant tubing and electrical construction materials serving HVAC and construction industries.
about:
Champlain Cable Corporation has operated from Plattsburgh, New York since its founding in 1946. The company remains privately held, though specific ownership details are not publicly disclosed. Over more than seven decades, it has grown into a specialist in high-performance wire and cable for demanding environments.

The company designs and manufactures copper and aluminum wire, tubing, and custom cable assemblies. Core processes include electron beam cross-linking, custom polymer compound development, advanced insulation systems, and collaborative design engineering. Champlain Cable maintains in-house irradiation treatment, testing, and research facilities, supported by a workforce of 50 to 199 employees. Product lines span building wire, refrigerant tubing, and branded solutions such as EXAR, EXRAD, DATACLEAR, and DATARAD.

Champlain Cable serves a diverse industrial base including automotive, aerospace, military, rail, truck and bus, industrial, marine, agricultural, mining, construction, and umbilicals markets. The company also supplies HVAC, plumbing, and electrical construction sectors. Notable customers include the U.S. Navy, for which it developed the DATACLEAR family of rugged, low-smoke data cables, and North American rail transit operators through a distribution partnership with Cameron Connect.

Champlain Cable emphasizes its leadership in irradiated cross-linked technology and polymer science, citing continuous investment in manufacturing innovation. The company states that its differentiators are custom product innovation, cutting-edge polymer science, in-house irradiation treatments, and rigorous testing and process controls, all aimed at delivering superior durability, flexibility, and thermal resistance for mission-critical applications.

name: Champlain Metals
old_description: Champlain Metals offers design and metal fabrication solutions for structural and ornamental metal work. John Marius carries on the old world passion for detail rooted in the traditions learned from working in the New York metropolitan area and the Champagne and Alsatian regions of France.
about:
Champlain Metals was founded in 2004 by John Marius in Burlington, Vermont. Marius, who trained with the French artisans’ guild Compagnons du Devoir, brought a tradition of ornamental metalwork learned in the Champagne and Alsatian regions of France to the Champlain Valley. The shop began as a one‑person operation and has served residential, commercial, and contractor clients across the region for over 15 years.

The company provides design, fabrication, casting, and forging services for structural and ornamental metalwork. Its capabilities include architectural metal work, custom metal fabrication, bronze and iron casting, and forging of components such as brackets, railings, and stair stringers. The shop states it can handle production runs, though specific facility size, headcount, or annual volume are not disclosed.

Champlain Metals works with architects, builders, and private clients on projects ranging from custom side tables and garden trowels to heat exchangers and forged bronze cap rails. Past projects include stair stringers for a contractor named Andrew Russel, a heat exchanger for a residential client, and ornamental brackets for awning installations. The firm’s portfolio also features forged bronze details and iron pour samples.

Marius emphasizes an “old world passion for detail” rooted in European guild training as the firm’s distinguishing characteristic. The business was started to continue that tradition of hand‑crafted metalwork in Vermont, offering both one‑off artistic pieces and repeatable production work.

The shop fabricates structural steel for commercial and industrial projects, producing items such as fabricated structural steel, joists and deck, stairs and handrail, simple bridges and bridge components. It also manufactures material‑handling and heavy‑duty weighing equipment, and runs a value‑added steel service center. The facility holds AISC certification and AWS Certified Welding Fabricator status, with welding procedures covering all joints, processes and positions.

Customers include commercial contractors, industrial firms, material‑handling and weighing equipment makers, and the West Virginia Department of Highways for bridge work. The company’s central location provides convenient interstate access and proximity to East Coast shipping ports.

Charleston Steel emphasizes quality, competitive pricing and on‑time delivery, backed by annual AISC evaluations and AWS audits. Its quality system is reviewed each year by Quality Management Company, LLC to verify personnel, equipment, procedures and commitment to a quality product.

about:
Charlie's Machine & Supply operates from Longmont, Colorado, supplying fresh-cut fruit and vegetable processing equipment. The company does not publish its founding year or ownership details, but it emphasizes a cumulative experience of over 100 years across its team. It began as a specialist in new and used machinery for produce processing, offering everything from individual machines to complete plant lines.

The company designs and manufactures a range of equipment for peeling, wedging, coring, slicing, dicing, washing, and drying fresh produce. Its product line includes apple wedgers, carrot and cucumber peelers, cabbage corers, industrial dryers, and food processors such as the Hallde RG-400i and RG-300i models. Over 90 percent of the equipment is manufactured in the United States, and the firm custom-engineers solutions from single units to full production lines.

Customers are primarily fresh-cut produce processors and food manufacturing plants that require reliable, high-throughput equipment for fruits and vegetables. The company's featured machines — such as the 4-Step Double Wash system, the Dual Air Apple & Onion Wedger, and the Large Vegetable Belt Cutter/Slicer — illustrate the focus on high-volume, automated processing.

Charlie's Machine & Supply differentiates itself through its 'CMS Guarantee,' which cites over 100 years of cumulative experience, highest standards in design and manufacturing, reliability, post-sale service, and a commitment to USA-made equipment. The company states that its service detail does not stop after the sale.
